threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the Overground.' Everyone else has already adapted to the clunky connections.
Heard a guy on the N35 boasting about his 'royal rum' stash while the bus jostled past the old cinema. Made me think, what's the craziest thing in a backpack?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was here when I saw a crowd laughing around an old man selling handmade soaps by the canal, weaving stories between his sales pitches.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here. Not just clubs, real DIY vibes. It's an experience that’s hard to find elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to skip the BART on Fridays; it's a mess with overheated brakes and delays. Tourists just fume in line.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a pet iguana on the Muni—he claimed it’s a service animal. Only in the Tenderloin would that get a nod from the driver.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think 'local' means a trendy brunch spot. In Gràcia, it's really about the neighborhood market where everyone knows your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You know they're new when they still stop to take selfies with the Gaudí buildings instead of just rolling their eyes.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube line status before leaving home—true locals know it's a gamble regardless.
Last night on the 196, a guy tried to sell a lost cat collar to everyone. Claimed it was 'vintage.' You can't make this stuff up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a street artist painting a mural of a cat on a traffic light while someone tried to sell homemade lemonade from a bicycle. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM with a line longer than a club's. It's the unofficial after-party scene, just with more tahini.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission when they can name three taquerias just from the scent of grilled onions wafting by.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Muni bus departed while a jogger tried to catch it—no sprinting. They stopped to catch their breath and kept running, like it was all just a part of the routine.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think Gràcia is all about the Gaudí and the parks, but it’s really the hidden plazas and local bars that have the heart of the neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they still take photos of the Diagonal’s traffic lights—like it’s some hidden gem, not just another boring crosswalk.
